name: Alternating Dumbbell Flat Bench Press
description: The Alternating Dumbbell Press is performed on a flat bench with one arm pressing while the other holds the dumbbell in a fixed position near the chest. The asymmetrical loading creates a significant anti-rotation demand on the core and obliques while one side presses. This variation also allows greater focus on each arm independently and can reveal strength imbalances between sides.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level with a neutral or pronated grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Start with both dumbbells at chest level. Begin with the non-dominant arm pressing first to identify any strength asymmetry.
steps: Step 1: Press one dumbbell up to lockout while keeping the other stationary at chest level.
Step 2: Lower the pressing arm back to the chest.
Step 3: Press the other arm while the first holds at chest level.
Step 4: Continue alternating for the prescribed reps per side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as each arm presses. Inhale as it returns to the chest.
common_mistakes: Letting the resting arm drift away from the body
Rotating the torso toward the pressing arm
safety_considerations: Keep the non-pressing arm safely resting at chest — do not let it fall to the side
Start with a lighter load than your standard dumbbell press
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension of pressing arm. Non-pressing arm held at 90 degrees of elbow flexion at chest level.
coaching_cues: Fight the rotation — your torso stays still
The resting arm is working too — keep it controlled
